dishes.name: Bouillabaisse
dishes.desc: The famous Marseille fish stew, a dish with centuries of history rooted in a humble Greek-style fishermen's stew. Served at the port as broth and fish together.

dishes.name: Navettes de Marseille
dishes.desc: Boat-shaped orange-blossom biscuits, the Marseille sweet best suited to taking home. They travel well and are sold in bakeries across the city.

dishes.name: Panisses
dishes.desc: Fried chickpea-flour fritters, a popular street snack in Marseille and especially associated with L'Estaque. Crisp outside, soft inside, and meat-free.

dishes.name: Pieds paquets
dishes.desc: Lamb tripe parcels stuffed with salted pork, garlic and parsley, simmered in white wine and tomato. A Marseille dish credited to a cook of La Pomme district in 1880.

dishes.name: Calissons d'Aix
dishes.desc: Almond-and-melon-paste sweets with a royal icing top, from Aix-en-Provence. One of the traditional thirteen desserts of a Provençal Christmas.

dishes.name: Chichis
dishes.desc: Sweet fried dough fritters, a traditional Marseille treat. Eaten warm, often in the L'Estaque district.
